x: ALISTAIR MORFEY.D.o.b. 24.5.60.Coached by Mick Dunphy. Dogged by knee injuries at Camb.Univ. where he graduated in Mech Eng Alistair has returne[illegible] to athletics this year following an abortive attempt at a world tour when he picked up a particularly dangerous strain of maleria in Kenya.
John Gladwin won the 800 in style and Stuart Paton won a hard 1500 having let a big gap develop.Alistair Morfey gained usefull points in the B 1500 and went through the 800 with Stu in 2mins dead.
Mark sinclair ran 1.56.3 in the 'B' 800m, Alistair Morfey ran 3.56.9 in the 1500m to finish just behind Gary Staines, Oliver Foote ran a 8.20.0 3000m.
Our other winners were new member Alistair Morfey in the 5000m, Mark Shippen in the Pole Vault and Mark Sinclair with a fine win in the 800m.

With Stu Paton and Gary Staines representing the SCAAA, Alistair Morfey running for Achilles and Paul Richley, Mark Sinclair plus Ken Onuagaluchi competing as guests this was very much a Belgrave night at the Palace.

A.Morfey 12.27,A.Gayton 13.46,S.Holmes 14.22.................. Teams; 1.H.H.H.H. 74.28*, 2.SLH 76.06, 3.Croydon 76.15.....10.BELGRAVE 82.22. *H.H.H. had two runners who managed to shorten the course but the referee decided that this did not affect the result which they let stand.
The race was won by Graham Tuck in 31.02 our first man home being Alistair Morfey in 11th place in 32.23 closely followed by Mike Hayes who finished in 13th position in 32.30.
